(2) SELL THE FULL TLT LONG (opened 2026-08-20 at 82.60) at market on the same open and KEEP the TLT short - the book holds both legs, nets to approximately zero, and pays spread and borrow to hold nothing.

HOUSEKEEPING, all in the watchlist: cancel five resting long limits sitting 8-14% below the market (VST, PFE, DG, CEG, LCII), two crypto shorts stale by 26% (BTC, /MBTU6), and all three Fed event-contract orders (two of which are YES on a hike and YES on a hold at the same meeting). EEM and DINO are inside a normal pullback and stand. This is one systematic habit, not seven separate misses: every long idea published in the second half of August was right about direction and never filled, because each entry was set below the market and the market went up. The XLE idea below raises its level rather than restating 63.00 for a fourth time.

HOW TO READ THE TWO EXIT ROWS (ranks 1 and 2). Both carry direction 'buy' because that is the side of the position being closed - a 'sell' row would open a NEW short in the tracker rather than amend the existing long, which is the opposite of the intent. Both have target, stop and reward-to-risk set to NULL on purpose: a flatten instruction has no levels. In LULU's case the 128.00 target and 93.50 stop the research phase attached to it were scaffolding constructed to demonstrate that no version of the trade clears the 2.0 floor from a filled 115.00 entry - they appear nowhere in the research as real levels, so publishing them would have been inventing prices. Conviction on these rows scores confidence in the CLOSE, not in a purchase.

IDEA COUNT: seven recommendations - two exits, one held short, three new swing entries and one long-term hold. There is no target count and nothing was padded or trimmed to reach one; this is everything that cleared. Ranks 1 and 2 are exits and are ranked by urgency rather than conviction; ranks 3-7 are ranked by conviction then recomputed reward-to-risk.

RATIO CLUSTERING - READ THIS BEFORE SIZING. Every swing idea recomputes just above its 2.0 floor: TLT short 2.06, FRO 2.14, XLE 2.13, ORCL 2.12. That clustering is the exact signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, and it is flagged rather than explained away. What can be said in its defence is that the other half of the test passes with room - stops are 2.61, 2.27, 2.75 and 2.09 ATR against floors of 1.8/2.0/1.8/2.0 - so the ratios are being held down by conservative targets rather than lifted by tight stops, which is the honest failure mode of the two. Treat 2.1 as 'barely clears', not as an edge.

CORRELATION - the concentration is real and is not an oversight. XLE, FRO and the TLT short all descend from one driver: the Hormuz energy shock feeding headline CPI feeding Fed-hike pricing. That is exactly 3 ideas, at the cap, and refiners, airlines, LNG and gas producers were rejected on those grounds rather than on merit. GLD is deliberately the other side of the same variable and says so in its own key_risk. If the Strait reopens next week, XLE and FRO both gap toward their stops, the TLT short loses its driver, and GLD is the only thing in the book that benefits.

GLD SUPERSESSION: an earlier note in the research log proposed cutting the GLD target from 520 to 462.21 with an SMA50 invalidation. The later captured candidate keeps 520 - named explicitly as a level (the January 2026 record), not a valuation, since gold has no cash flows - and adds the invalidation the original position lacked. The candidate is the later decision and is what is published; the reader should know 520 is above the 180-day high of 509.70.

market_context.summary:
The single most important fact today: the market has stopped pricing a Fed that cuts and started pricing one that HIKES. Kalshi has the Sep 16 FOMC at 49/50c for a 25bp hike against 48/50c for a hold and 0/1c for ANY cut, on real open interest (9.85M contracts on the hold bucket alone), and by December it has more hike than hold priced cumulatively. The cash market says the same thing independently: the 2-year at 4.34% sits 71bp ABOVE the 3.63% effective funds rate, with the 10-year at 4.77% and the curve positively sloped by 41bp. Consensus positioning built through 2025-26 was 'the Fed cuts eventually'; that is not what is priced anymore.

The mechanism is energy, and this is the report's most useful single observation: headline CPI YoY was 3.30% in July while core was 2.47%, and the market prices August at 3.3% headline against 2.3-2.4% core - a ~95bp gap it expects to WIDEN. Retail gasoline averaged $3.92 in August, +3.2% m/m, with WTI at 91.48 on Sep 1 after the US-Iran escalation closed the Strait of Hormuz. So the Fed is priced roughly 50/50 to hike on a headline number produced by an oil supply shock while core sits near target. Central banks conventionally look through supply shocks; Chair Warsh is explicitly not, on credibility grounds, having said on ~Aug 28 that underlying inflation has not 'meaningfully improved'. Whatever one thinks of that, it is the fault line every trade today sits on, and Sep 11 CPI is the trigger that resolves it.

The tape itself is dull and coiled: SPY 770.19, 1.18% off its high, twenty sessions spent between 761.78 and 777.88 on a 0.71% ATR. Energy is the outright leader (XLE +10.1% on the month against SPY +0.2%), gold is 21.8% below its January record on the same rate repricing, and BTC at 79,627 is down ~9% year to date and mid-range. Underneath it, the consumer is being squeezed by the same energy shock - seven of the eleven small caps screened are consumer discretionary and every one is deeply de-rated, LULU itself at an 8-year low. The energy longs here and the consumer wreckage are two ends of one transfer, so do not read the Sep 9-10 retail earnings cluster as independent of the oil trade.

catalyst.event: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed after the Sep 1 US-Iran escalation and the reimposition of the US naval blockade in early August. WTI went 84.57 to 91.48 between Aug 28 and Sep 1 (FRED DCOILWTICO); Brent 91.05. Qatar-Oman mediation has not produced a deal and vessel transits are down to about five a day.
catalyst.action: enter on the next open. The condition that would make this wrong is a signed reopening agreement - if one is announced, exit rather than wait for the stop, because the gap will be through it.

recommendations.thesis: Oil has repriced on the Hormuz escalation and energy equities have only partly followed: over the same five sessions USO rose 9.45% while XLE rose 2.20%, leaving USO 14.6% above its 50-day average and XLE only 8.2% above its own. This is the same trade as the Frontline idea at a much lower point on the risk curve - a $1.7bn-a-day ETF sitting 2.2% below its 120-day high rather than a single shipowner 272% above its lows - and it is the cleaner way to be long the energy shock if only one is taken.
recommendations.key_risk: A Hormuz reopening deal, which has been described as close since Aug 5 and would take the war premium out of crude overnight and gap XLE straight through the 60.80 stop. Secondarily, this is a bet that equities catch up to the commodity, and the historical record for that is mixed: energy equities discount a mean-reverting oil price on purpose, so part of the 7-point gap is correct pricing rather than a lag to be harvested. RED TEAM, two risks absent from this list. First, a war premium does not need a peace deal to come out: a coordinated IEA/SPR release or an OPEC+ spare-capacity response is the standard official answer to a supply shock, arrives without warning, and would gap XLE through 60.80 with the strait still shut - so the stated invalidation covers only one of the two ways this loses. Second, after the FRO cut this book still holds two legs on the one Hormuz headline: this long and the TLT short, which needs the same energy-driven CPI to keep the Fed hiking. A reopening takes both down together. GLD is the only position that gains on that outcome. Conviction comes down from 4 to 3 because the edge is consensus rather than thin: energy is the outright leading sector at +10.1% on the month, the USO-versus-XLE gap is five sessions old and visible to every desk, and this idea's own counter-argument concedes part of that gap is correct pricing rather than a lag to harvest. Note also that the 2.13:1 ratio depends on a 70.50 target 7.6% above the 120-day high - defensible for a leading sector breaking out, but measured to the 65.52 high instead the ratio is about 0.5:1.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the gap is the market being right. A war premium is the least durable component of an oil price, XLE constituents will not sanction new supply against it, and the 2026 pattern of three failed de-escalations cuts both ways - each previous escalation also reversed. On top of that XLE is already 2.2% from its 120-day high after a 10% month, so this is not a depressed asset; it is a strong one being asked to get stronger.

Gold does not need to return to a price set under a completely different rate regime. The honest reply is only that the fiscal driver is unchanged and the position is +2.2% - not that the bear case is wrong.

watchlist.note: CUT by the red team on the correlation test. The XLE idea's own thesis says it is "the same trade as the Frontline idea at a much lower point on the risk curve" and "the cleaner way to be long the energy shock IF ONLY ONE IS TAKEN" - and then the report took both, 2% plus 3% on one Hormuz headline with an identical invalidation on each. Nothing here says the thesis is wrong; it says it is already owned through XLE.
watchlist.trigger: Take FRO instead of XLE only if the pair is re-underwritten as one slot, not two. A pullback into the 42-43 SMA20 area with the strait still shut would make the single-name version pay for its extra risk; buying 2% off a 400-day high does not.
